card.name: Linking words after biology or drug nouns
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as 'of', 'from', 'for' or an opening bracket right after a biochemical or drug noun, like 'decomposition of', 'derived from' or 'antidepressants for'. Also some spots inside gene-name expansions.

modes.label: Link word before a source or use
modes.description: A preposition after a process, derived-substance or drug-class noun, leading into the thing it applies to.
modes.example: It is produced during the decomposition<< of>> a larger protein, APP.

modes.label: Antidepressants for the condition
modes.description: The word 'for' after 'antidepressants' in boxed-warning text, before major depressive disorder.
modes.example: adolescents, and young adults taking antidepressants<< for>> major depressive disorder and other psychiatric disorders.

modes.label: Gene name expansions
modes.description: An opening bracket or a piece of the spelled-out name right after a gene symbol.
